basics.name: Pedro Fontanarrosa
basics.label: Bioinformatics & ML Scientist | Microbiome Modeling, PINNs, Reproducible AI
basics.summary: PhD-trained computational biologist with 7+ years building and scaling AI/ML models on biological data (microbiome & gene-expression time series), with a focus on reproducible pipelines, rigorous QC, and transparent documentation. Deep Python stack (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, PyMC), strong time-series and mechanistic modeling (gLV, VAR, PINNs), and HPC experience. Comfortable translating stakeholder questions into computational plans, iterating quickly, and communicating results clearly to non-statisticians.

work.name: Computational Systems & Synthetic Biology Lab, University College London
work.summary: Developed and maintained Python packages and ML pipelines for simulating, inferring, and predicting microbial community dynamics from noisy omics time series. Led hybrid ML–mechanistic modeling (PINNs, gray-box) to improve interpretability and parameter recovery. Ensured reproducibility (unit tests, docs, CI/CD) and HPC scalability.
highlights: Authored a PINN benchmarking preprint on accuracy and uncertainty quantification for gLV inference (DeepXDE, ensembles, MC-dropout).
Designed and published MIMIC, integrating gLV/VAR/consumer–resource models with Bayesian inference for microbiome dynamics.
Built train/eval stacks in Python (NumPy/pandas/scikit-learn), DL (PyTorch/TensorFlow), and visualization (matplotlib/seaborn).
Implemented robust data cleaning and harmonization for multi-omic matrices; added imputation for irregular time points.
Wrote clear READMEs, analysis reports, and docstrings; enforced code quality via Git, code review, and CI.
Executed workloads on UCL HPC (SLURM), containerized with Docker for reproducible runs.

work.name: Genetic Logic Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
work.summary: Mathematical modeling and Genetic Design Automation in synthetic biology; improved simulation accuracy and forecasting of gene-circuit dynamics; collaborated across wet-lab and computational teams.
highlights: Enhanced tooling (e.g., iBioSim) and models for gene-circuit design and analysis.
Authored peer-reviewed publications; supported cross-functional data analysis and interpretation.
Contributed to reproducible workflows and version-controlled analysis assets.
